correctness.rationale: Dominy et al. Lemma 5 was checked in the open full text and gives the exact eigenvalue for one weak stabilizer measurement on every isotypical sector. Composition over a schedule multiplies these diagonal eigenvalues, producing the Hamming weight of the associated binary word. Orthogonality of the sectors then makes the restricted Hilbert--Schmidt norm the largest residual eigenvalue, equal to the code minimum-distance exponent. Rank-deficient schedules leave a nontrivial sector fixed. Endpoint and intermediate examples were independently enumerated by the bundled checker. The proof is analytic; finite enumeration is not used to justify the general quantifiers.
risks: The exact norm statement is for the nonselective measurement layer in the Hilbert--Schmidt geometry; it does not by itself provide an exact full system--bath trace-distance error after interleaved dynamics.
Unequal measurement strengths would replace ordinary Hamming weight by a weighted exponent and are outside the stated claim.

originality.rationale: The closest prior strands were separated statement-by-statement. The Zeno source gives the single-stabilizer eigenvalue and two endpoint schedules but not arbitrary schedule optimization. Data-syndrome work uses classical linear codes to make selective syndrome outcomes robust to classical readout errors, while the 2024 code-inspired measurement paper treats robust projective measurements. None of the inspected sources states that the nonselective weak-measurement channel has isotypical spectrum indexed by codeword weights or that its worst Hilbert--Schmidt contraction is exactly the classical minimum distance. Classical code parameters themselves are explicitly excluded from novelty.
residual_risks: The 2014 conference paper on robust syndrome extraction was available primarily through abstract/bibliographic material in this check; its later comprehensive treatment arXiv:1907.01393 was inspected in full.
An unindexed paper may explicitly connect weak nonselective stabilizer attenuation to syndrome-measurement code distance.
The theorem does not claim novelty for syndrome-measurement codes, projective robust measurement coding, or any classical minimum-distance value.

value.rationale: The source presents a sharp resource tension between measuring only generators and measuring the exponentially larger full stabilizer group. The finding fills that motivated gap with an exact continuum of intermediate schedules and converts worst-sector suppression at fixed elementary-measurement budget into a mature coding-theory invariant. The r=3 example shows a concrete nontrivial gain: one extra distinct stabilizer squares the worst attenuation factor. This is a structural design lemma for weak stabilizer control, not a recomputation of a known code table.
risks: The physical cost of a product stabilizer can exceed the cost of a generator, so elementary measurement count is only one resource model.
The theorem addresses the measurement layer; translating the improved contraction exponent into a sharp full dynamical error bound is future work.
sources: arXiv:1207.5880 explicitly contrasts full-group and generator-only WMQZE protocols and notes the resource saving of the latter.
arXiv:1907.01393 and DOI:10.1038/s41534-024-00904-y establish the independent practical relevance of code-designed redundant measurements.
